steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place apples in an 8x8 inch baking dish. Toss apples with syrup. In a separate bowl, mix together flour, oats, sugar, and salt. Cut in butter until mixture is crumbly. Sprinkle mixture evenly over apples.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35 minutes, until topping is golden brown. Serve warm or at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Maple Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: Sliced apples are slathered in syrup, arranged in a baking dish and covered with a wonderful crumble made from brown sugar, butter and rolled oats. The crisp is then baked and served warm with scoops of rum raisin ice cream.
raw_recipe.name: Maple Apple Crisp

review.reviewBody: We loved this. I did REDUCE the amount of butter to ONLY 1/4 cup, that maybe why some reviewers gave a lower rating because it was to soggy. Reduce the amount of butter & it will turn out Perfect! I also added 1/2 t. cinnamon and 1/2 t. nutmeg to topping when mixing it. This is a keeper!

Loved this over all. Used my own maple syrup. I simmered the apples, maple syrup, with a quarter cup of water in a saucepan for about 15 minutes. It made the apples tender and reduced the syrup so the inside wasn't "soupy" as others mentioned. Added a bit of cinnamon to the topping. It was delicious.

This was super easy to make and very tasty! I think the serving size is way off though. The first time I made this in an 8x8, the servings would have been way to small to feed 8 people. Also, I think the baking time is off...needs to bake longer so it isn't mushy and so the top coating gets crunchy/crisp. I added more apples and made in an 9x13 this past time...and it was great. I served it with french vanilla ice cream while it was still hot. YUM!

My family loves this. I use 8 apples and bake it in a 9x13 pan. I use 3/4 cup each of the brown sugar, oats and flour and only 1/4 cup of butter (to reduce fat). I cook it about 45 minutes to brown the top. Don't have any problem with it being soupy.

This was simple and delicious. All I had was gala apples on hand and it still turned out great. I just drizzled the maple syrup over the apples once I put them in the dish instead of using the measured amount. I added chopped walnuts and a handful of flax seeds to the crust mixture. Also topped it off with a dusting of cinnamon before baking. Apples have a lot of water in them, so expect the juice to cook out. That's just part of it, and it makes a good drizzle over ice cream.

I love this recipe. Thank you! I’ve made it several times. I need to try it with less sugar, less syrup and less butter next time. It’s the only way I eat apples! I use Granny Smith. I use whole wheat flour but will shift to a gluten free flour. I added walnuts and currents and cinnamon.

This turned out very good! I had gala apples I needed to use that weren't the sweetest to begin with, so I doubted this recipe would turn out. I thought there was too much syrup once I put it with the apples so I added some brown sugar and a little of the crubmle to the mix (I also used light pancake syrup not the real-deal, maple syrp). Also threw in some cinnamon and splenda on top before adding the crumble topping. For the crumble I added wheat germ, ground flax seed and subed 1/4 a cup of whole wheat flour to 1/4 of enriched. I think if I make this again I'll put less syrup or add a little cornstarch to thicken it a bit. Or maybe splurge on real maple syrup! I think it would be really good with some nuts sprinkled on top too. Maybe dried cranberries or a little something else mixed in as well. Overall really good!

I think this is a very great basic recipe! I made just a couple simple modifications and it was truly fantastic.

I know I like a generous amount of "crisp" topping, so i used 3/4 cup each of the flour, oats and brown sugar. I also added 1 tsp baking powder to the flour. I kept the butter at 1/2 cup. 

I sprinkled the apples with about a tbsp of corn starch, then tossed them with the maple syrup. Helped to thicken all the juices a little I think. I then sprinkled a tbsp or so of cinnamon over the apples before pressing the oat topping lightly over the apples. yumm

This was a simple and nice apple dessert (tastes great with vanilla ice cream!). My only problem was the cooking time. I cooked it for 40 minutes, but I think next time I'll put it in for more like 50-60 minutes. My apples weren't very soft and my "crisp" not very cooked after 35 minutes (disclaimer: i'm at altitude--cooking is weird here). I thought 1/2 cup (instead of the 3/4 cup) of real maple syrup was a perfect amount, but I regret having cut the butter down to 1/4 cup as was recommended by so many reviewers. Next time I'll stick with the 1/2 cup (it wasn't bad with 1/4, but I think the crisp would have a nicer texture and taste with the full amount). I also dropped a little cinnamon into the crisp, which I thought was a nice addition. I used gala apples and those worked fine--next time I might mix fuji and granny smiths and see how that tastes. I'll be making this one again.

Made this today, i tastes sooo good! 
I did make a few changes though. My spouse doesn't like oats in a crisp topping, so I left it out and doubled the flour. I added 1/2c chopped walnuts and 1/2 tsp cinnamon to the topping, plus 1/2c dried cranberries to the apples. 
 I cut the maple syrup to 1/2c based on other reviews, but still got a runny crisp. 
Even though I reduced the amount of syrup, I still got a nice maple flavor. Probably because I used real, Vermont-made, grade A Dark Amber maple syrup, which has more intense flavor than lighter grades. 
Next time, I will dredge the apples in flour before adding the syrup and topping. Hopefully that will thicken the excess juice. 
And I will skip the cranberries and cinnamon, as I didn't really taste them. The predominant flavor was a lovely combo of apples, maple, and buttery streusel. And that's more than enough.

This recipe is absolutely delish! When I first made this it came out real runny, still tasty, but I prefer a thick apple crisp. So after I chop up my apples, I always use granny smith, I toss them in cornstarch before putting the maple syrup & topping on. It really helps to soak up the juices and give it a thicker texture. Another twist to this recipe I sometimes do is add 2 cups of fresh blueberries with only 3 apples and it is just as delish if not better!! I call it Maple Appleberry Crisp!! Just made one tonight, hubby's been begging me ever since our local farm started putting out the fresh picked blueberries!
Very easy
Just delicious and wonderful as a dessert or for breakfast!
Apples still crunchy, needs cinnamon, maple syrup just made it watery

I read many of the reviews with all the changes that were made, but I stayed true to the recipe as written. The consistency was not soupy, it actually was just about perfect. A little sweet for our taste, so I will cut back a bit on both the maple syrup and brown sugar in the future. Satisfied with the way this turned out.
It's very good, however, I think next time I'd skip the brown sugar. With the maple syrup, it plenty sweet enough. And/or cut the maple syrup in half. Debbie S.
Yummy! A little too sweet!

I made as written with Gala apples. Very sweet, granny Smith apples would be my choice next time. I served at room temperature as directed and that is definitely the way to go. It was a tad soupy, I may add Knox gelatin to the apple mixture, if I make it again. Or, I may reduce the butter which will help reduce soupy consistency. Overall, I think it’s a good recipe. Two of us can’t eat it all at once so in the fridge overnight it goes and then letting it sit at room temperature In day .The extra soupiness is keeping it moist.
Tasty and easy to make. Cinnamon ice cream on top .l
I made it for my card group, and they loved it. Someone asked me for the recipe. I used my own maple syrup.
